chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim from Ja'far from his father (peace be upon him) who said:

Imam Ali (peace be upon him) said regarding the making up of the month of Ramadan: If one is unable to perform it continuously, one should divide it. And he said: One does not make up the month of Ramadan during the ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah. The meaning of this report regarding his statement 'one does not make up the month of Ramadan during the ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah' is that we interpret it as applying to one who is a pilgrim, because he will be traveling. And it is not permissible for the traveler to make up the month of Ramadan unless he stays in a town and intends to remain there for ten days or more. And that which indicates this is what we have previously mentioned from the reports regarding the permissibility of making up the month of Ramadan during Dhu al-Hijjah. As for that which indicates that it is not permissible to make up the month of Ramadan while traveling...

key_terms.عَشَرَةٌ مِنْ ذِي الْحِجَّةِ: The first ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah
key_terms.قَضَاءُ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: Making up the missed days of Ramadan

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for making up missed Ramadan fasts during the ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) clarifies that the prohibition on making up the entire month of Ramadan during the first ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah specifically applies to pilgrims in a state of travel, as they cannot fulfill the continuous fasting requirement while journeying. This ruling is contextualized by the principle that a traveler may only perform Qada in this period if they establish residence (Iqamah) for at least ten days, thereby transitioning from a traveler to a resident status. This distinction highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the interplay between travel status and ritual obligations during the sacred days of Dhu al-Hijjah.
